clue.text: Garment seen on the street as something flashy

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
a long loose outer garment

explanation.surface: Somebody spots a showy outfit being worn out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means the garment comes after the street, so the street abbreviation leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe light gives rapid bright pulses, so it is literally an item that flashes repeatedly.

clue.text: Like a sort of gun observed, something dramatic and very loud

blocks.note: saw means observed
Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese drama
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A gun is spotted in a loud, theatrical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: No (or Noh) is the stylised Japanese theatre form, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun with its barrel cut short is described by this term, so it is a type of gun.

clue.text: See 22
Good quality house ware at home - taken outside, broken on beach!

indicators.note: something broken is smashed to pieces, so the letters are put back in a new order
the phrase for home is put inside, with the other letters taken around its outside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
in means at home

explanation.surface: Fine crockery brought out of the house gets smashed on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: IN sits inside the jumbled letters of on beach, just before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is fine translucent porcelain made with bone ash, high-quality tableware for the home.

clue.text: Arab fellow, say?

blocks.note: surface reading: a man from Arabia
setter's reading: a creature that is part Arab horse and part fellow, half beast and half man

explanation.walkthrough: An Arab is also a breed of horse, and 'fellow' is a man; put them together and you get the mythical horse-man.
explanation.definitionFit: The creature of Greek myth has a human head and torso joined to the body of a horse.

clue.text: Jock's stool sounds scary

indicators.note: sounds says the word is judged by how it is heard, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: creepy means scary

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's seat makes eerie noises.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a creepie is a low wooden footstool, once used in church as a stool of repentance.

clue.text: Girl Irish missionary's upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: St Aidan, the Irish monk who evangelised Northumbria from Lindisfarne

explanation.surface: A young woman tells of an Irish missionary who is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a female first name, and girl stands for any female forename in crosswords.

clue.text: Country spot remembered by poet may get a little rain - shelter in case

indicators.note: something that shelters another holds it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a drop is a tiny amount of rain
lest means in case

explanation.surface: A rural spot recalled in verse may see a light shower, so bring an umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' tempts as a container indicator, but 'in case' is a single conjunction meaning for fear that; 'shelter' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adlestrop is a Gloucestershire village whose railway halt Edward Thomas immortalised in his poem of that name.

clue.text: Preceding T (29) is R (king, an old drunk) ...

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy old monarch is part of a cryptic list of initials.
explanation.walkthrough: With 8 down, this spells out the poet R S Thomas: R stands for this name, S for the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh poet R S Thomas was Ronald Stuart Thomas, so his first initial stands for this forename.

clue.text: ... associated with S (Scottish royal house)

blocks.note: first meaning: the middle name that the poet's S initial stands for
second meaning: the dynasty that ruled Scotland and later England

explanation.walkthrough: This continues 7 down: the poet R S Thomas was Ronald Stuart Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's second initial stands for this name, which is also the dynasty of Mary Queen of Scots and James I.

clue.text: To go round Thailand's capital, we get on a rickety carriage

indicators.note: a capital is the head of something, so only the opening letter of the country is kept
something rickety is shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
to go round something is to encircle it, so the jumbled letters surround the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the country's opening letter

explanation.surface: A tourist party climbs aboard a shaky old vehicle to tour Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Bangkok, but it only means the first letter. The anagram does not include it: the jumbled letters are built around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with facing side seats behind the driver.

clue.text: Bob is 29

blocks.note: first meaning: the American singer-songwriter Bob of that surname
second meaning: the Welsh poet whose first name goes with the surname at 29 across

explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is THOMAS, so the second half is the forename of the poet Dylan Thomas; the singer took his stage name from him.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves as the singer's adopted surname and as the Welsh poet Thomas's forename.

clue.text: Eye may be twitching after work

indicators.note: after places the twitching second, behind the word for a piece of work

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: Someone's eyelid starts to twitch after a long day at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After work' puts the twitch second; OP is a common crossword abbreviation for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a dated or jocular term for the organ of sight, and also relates to vision generally.

clue.text: Academician is exposed in shock survey

indicators.note: placing something in another word puts it inside, so the academician and is sit within the shock

blocks.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A member of the Royal Academy is caught out in a shocking scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts; with IS it goes into the middle of APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment or evaluation, much as a survey assesses a property's value and condition.

clue.text: Enthusiast's hand grabbing tot

indicators.note: a hand that grabs something closes around it, so one word holds the other inside

blocks.note: a clenched hand
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A keen fan's hand snatches up a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb, as in tot up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A faddist zealously follows the latest craze, an eager devotee of passing fashions.

clue.text: Setter-off observed climbing a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: noted means observed
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone sets off and is seen climbing up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter-off' sounds like a walker, but it is a device that sets off an explosion; a tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that triggers an explosive charge, the thing that sets off the blast.

clue.text: The 29 of 6

blocks.note: surface reading: an obscure cross-reference to two other entries
setter's reading: the poet named Thomas (29 across) who wrote the poem about the village at 6 down

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Thomas wrote the well-known poem Adlestrop, about a train stopping at a Cotswold station.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet surnamed Thomas who wrote the famous railway-station poem had this forename.

clue.text: A high street name of material significance

blocks.note: wool is a material for cloth
worth means value or importance

explanation.surface: A shop name with real weight in the textile trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material significance' reads as real importance, but it splits into a fabric and its value. Woolworths was a famous British high-street store chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolworth was the founder's surname and a long-standing chain store found on British high streets.

clue.text: See 22
What one's doing with extremes of lethargy at home and spirit sinking?

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends of a word, so only its outermost letters are kept
in a down entry sinking means going to the bottom, so the spirit comes last

blocks.note: the first and last letters of lethargy
in means at home
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A lazy day at home, sinking a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinking' says the spirit goes at the bottom of this down entry; the whole picture of idling at home with a drink is the lie-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in stays in bed late in the morning, which is what the lethargic drinker is doing.

clue.text: Lie from little wife, one going mad?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
one who is hopping mad, very angry

explanation.surface: A husband hears a tall tale from his small, furious wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopping mad' means furious, so the one doing it is jokily a hopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a colloquial word for a big, blatant untruth.

clue.text: Coming to victory holding top two cards - good!

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a win is a victory
ace and king, the two highest cards
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A card player wins while holding ace and king, a fine hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games the ace normally ranks above the king, so the top two cards are those two.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to means regaining consciousness, which is a sense of waking.

clue.text: Hesitation about having colour put on very big screen

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for hesitation is read the other way

blocks.note: er is a sound of hesitation
a colour
OS is outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A huge cinema screen has its colour adjusted after some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very big screen' looks like one phrase; the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen or partition behind a church altar.

clue.text: Girl sets non-U fashions

indicators.note: non-U says without the letter U, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a girl's name
puts means sets or places

explanation.surface: A young woman designs clothes that are not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class; here it just removes U from PUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or modify it, so adapts works as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Be inconsiderate fools, having grabbed diamonds, OK? That's 10's advice

annotation.answer: DON'T THINK TWICE RIGHT IT'S ALL

blocks.clueFragment: Be inconsiderate fools, having grabbed diamonds
blocks.note: how reckless fools behave when snatching jewels: acting without a moment's hesitation
OK means everything is fine; the grid places the last word of the phrase first

explanation.surface: Thieves who grab the gems are told to stop worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is an instruction to act without hesitating, as careless fools grabbing diamonds would; 10 across is Bob Dylan. The song title ends with the phrase for OK, its last word entered at 2 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the title of a 1963 Bob Dylan song, so it is literally advice from that singer.

clue.text: See 22
This could contribute to a solution

definitions.text: This could contribute to a solution

blocks.clueFragment: This could contribute to a solution
blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps solve a problem

blocks.clueFragment: This could contribute to a solution
blocks.note: setter's reading: the liquid in which a chemical solution is made, by dissolving something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' suggests the answer to a puzzle, but it is a liquid with something dissolved in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The common solvent dissolves salts and sugars, forming most everyday chemical solutions.

clue.text: Convey male image in tribe

blocks.note: to tote is to carry
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Someone carries a man's likeness in a tribal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or carved representation revered by a clan as its symbol.

clue.text: "Dishy" fellow in the lab

blocks.note: surface reading: an attractive man working in a laboratory
setter's reading: the scientist whose name is attached to a shallow laboratory dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishy' means attractive, but here it points to the culture dish named after the German bacteriologist Julius Richard Petri.
explanation.definitionFit: The German bacteriologist gave his name to the shallow lidded glass dish used for growing cultures.

clue.text: Produced singin' (and dancin') star highly thought of

blocks.note: Gene Kelly, star of the musical Singin' in the Rain
rated means esteemed, regarded well

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance star of the movies is held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g's point to the film Singin' in the Rain and its star Gene Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to create or bring into being, so generated is a synonym for made or produced.

clue.text: Rush in operation - when this person's busy

definitions.text: Rush in operation - when this person's busy

blocks.note: a surge is a sudden rush
on means working, in operation

explanation.surface: A hectic dash in the operating theatre is when this person is at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes someone who is busy during an operation in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical specialist who operates is busiest in theatre, rushing during a procedure.

clue.text: Biblical "twin", or one of three here?

blocks.note: first meaning: the apostle called Didymus, which means twin
second meaning: the surname of three poets in this puzzle, Dylan, Edward and R S

explanation.walkthrough: The doubting apostle was also called Didymus, Greek for twin. The puzzle's poets are Dylan, Edward and Ronald Stuart Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle and the three Welsh-linked poets in this grid all share the one name.
